paper.title: GrIPS: Gradient-free, Edit-based Instruction Search for Prompting Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: GrIPS, a gradient-free phrase-level edit search over task instructions scored on a small labeled set, improves instructions for LLMs including API-only models, outperforming manual rewriting and example-prompt search at matched budget and comparable to select gradient-based tuning.

signatures.object: Natural-language task instruction inside a fixed prompt template (one per task/model/seed).
signatures.information: Score-set labels via label log-probabilities (balanced accuracy + entropy); test labels unseen; API-only access.
signatures.operation: Parse phrases → sample one edit (delete/swap/paraphrase/add) for 5 candidates → score → accept best if strictly better → patience 2, ≤10 iterations; optional beam/annealing.
signatures.conditions: Instruction-sensitive model; 20–100 labeled examples; classification with label probabilities.
signatures.feedback: Score-set accuracy and label entropy of the candidate.
signatures.selection_rule: Strict improvement over incumbent; beam keeps top-B.
signatures.persistence: Final instruction string; no cross-task library.
signatures.later_use: Applied to held-out test examples of the same task.
signatures.failure_boundary: Returns original instruction when no improvement; gains shrink with smaller score sets; cannot add new information; classification only.

gap.author_gap: Manual rewriting is slow/subjective; gradient prompt tuning is costly, unavailable for API models and unreadable.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete for the 2021–22 literature; readability advantage partly contradicted by incoherent searched instructions.
gap.residue: Edits cannot add information; gains model/task dependent.
gap.stakes: Improve API-model prompts with a small labeled set.
gap.method_response: Greedy/beam local search over phrase edits.
gap.remaining_gap: Generative tasks, largest models, interpretation of incoherent edits, label-bias vs understanding.

rs_pattern.reason: Load-bearing operation is black-box hill-climbing over discrete phrase edits of one text artifact against a labeled score set. Checked and rejected: generative_process_redesign (sol) — its liberated components belong to iterative/staged generative procedures; the instruction is the model's input, and 'free a fixed component' would then cover any optimizer; adapt_via_conditioning (checked by Opus) — operation is expressing new tasks as conditioning for cross-task generalization with structural holdout, while GrIPS performs per-task labeled search over the conditioning text; reframe_as_solvable_object, assumption_audit_and_pivot, architectural_operator_substitution (son55's reasons hold); relax_discrete_search_to_continuous — GrIPS stays discrete. Fully evaluated regardless.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: gains on API models without gradients for some tasks; readability goal often not met.

claims.text: GrIPS improves average accuracy (GPT-2 XL +9.36, babbage +4.29, curie +2.36).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Significant average gains on this task set; two of three models end near/below the majority-label level, so task-understanding gains are not separated from label-bias correction.

claims.text: Beats manual rewriting and exemplar search at matched budget.
claims.baseline_control: Authors' manual rewrite; matched-query example search.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Matched-query advantage of 1.5–1.6 points on InstructGPT; GPT-2 XL example search wins.

claims.setting: GPT-2 XL, 80:20 split of score set.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Greedy below finetuning; beam at ~B-fold queries exceeds it; compute unmatched.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Retained instruction improves held-out examples of the same task; no improver-level claim.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Greedy phrase-edit search on a 100-example score set yields instructions that raise held-out accuracy on 8 binary tasks and beat matched-query exemplar search on InstructGPT; part of the gain may be label-bias correction and the readability advantage is not supported.

G.reason: Specific gap (API-only black-box models, subjective manual rewriting, unreadable gradient prompts) positioned against rewriting, prompt tuning and prompt search with a matched-query baseline; readability residue undercut by incoherent outputs.

M.reason: Local phrase edits + strict-improvement acceptance + entropy-augmented fitness, with ablations of each piece; why gains occur (calibration vs semantics) is open.

X.reason: Pseudocode for greedy/beam/annealing, operators, parser, hyperparameters, stopping and failure behaviour are reconstructable; incumbent kept unless strictly better. Not 4: the commit gate reuses the proposal score set (100 examples) with no noise margin, and hyperparameter-tuning data are unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Gold-label accuracy with CIs on 300 examples/task, but two of three models end at/below the 59.83 majority-label level on partly skewed test sets while the fitness rewards label diversity; test label distributions are not reported, so 'task improvement' vs label-bias correction is not separable.

E.causality.reason: No-search, matched-query example search, authors' manual rewrite, gradient baselines and op/entropy ablations exist; but the strongest alternative (calibration/label-bias correction) and a random-edit/best-of-N control are untested, and gradient/beam comparisons are compute-unmatched.

E.holdout.reason: Score set disjoint from 300-example test; FLAN-T5 exposure flagged; no cross-task claim. Hyperparameter-tuning data unstated; one benchmark family.

E.statistics.reason: 3–5 seeds, bootstrap CIs and p<0.05 tests, per-task win counts and failure cases; ablations on 100 examples lack intervals.

E.cost.reason: Evaluation-count formula, per-seed and total dollars, matched-query example search; beam and gradient baselines not compute-matched.

Specification is complete (son55's basis), but the domain's first X check is the retention gate: commits use the same 100-example score set as proposals with a strict '>' and no noise margin (H31-disjoint partial), and hyperparameter-tuning data are unstated. Anchor 4 needs selection/retention conditions clear and sound → 3.

Verified Table 1: majority label 59.83; GPT-2 XL ends at 58.90 and babbage at 60.09 (CI ±3.7). With an entropy term rewarding label diversity and partly skewed test sets, the accuracy gain is not shown to be task improvement rather than label-bias correction; sol did not address this.

Baselines/ablations are real, but the strongest alternative explanation (calibration / label-bias) has no control, nor does random editing at equal queries; anchor 4–3 requires strong alternatives tested.

aggregate_review.initial_judgment_before_seat_scores: B-class prompt optimizer: edit search with strict-improvement acceptance, score set vs disjoint test → retained (same-task). Strengths: CIs, bootstrap, seeds, budget-matched example search, costs. Concern spotted on first read: GPT-2 XL+GrIPS below the majority-label baseline and babbage ≈ majority, with an entropy term in the fitness.
